details:
Hello. I've been playing VRChat for decent amount of time and I really do enjoy the game and see lots of potential in it. The latest few updates have done some great things for the game. I wanted to give my input as a player on some features I think may be good to implement moving forward. 

First off, I play on an Oculus and have talked to friends of mine who use Vive about this. Both Oculus and Vive have buttons on the controllers that are completely unused (not sure which it is exactly on Vive but for Oculus A, X and pressing in the left thumbstick all have no use in game.) and so we would love to see an update in which VR users can use one of the free controls to have push to talk like desktop users have. It's something that would really be helpful for VR users who live in a loud home environment such as near an airport, or they just have a barking dog, or whatever. Point is, having to go into the system menu to mute yourself temporarily for that  kind of sucks. If this does get implemented though, it would be best to make it optional because I obviously can't speak for everyone, and I can see how constant mic transmission could be desirable for some users. 

The next feature my friends and I have discussed is a bit simpler. With the new safety mode feature to block all avatars, it would be nice if people who have that mode turned on would appear with a little symbol next to their nameplate to indicate that they have it turned on like how you get the ear with the X through it if someone has you muted. I've had multiple occasions where I've started talking with someone in game and gone to show them a cool animation or new avatar I've made only for me to explain it as I show it and them then tell me they can't see any of it because they have avatars blocked. 

Next, on the topic of the new particle update (I have seen it was temporarily removed.) If you do want to still implement that, I think that it should also be an optional feature. A lot of how much someone can handle particle effects comes down to their own PC and so for people like myself who are on higher end PC builds, it's not fair to limit the game visually just because some people can't run it. Easiest fix for both sides in my opinion is to make it an option, not a forced feature for everyone. 

That's really it for now. Nothing else stands out to me as an issue that hasn't already been fixed. I love the home system, and the new cameras, and the ability to toggle HUD and nameplates from the menu is perfect. Thank you for your time and continued work on the game.
title: A few feature suggestions.
